newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bulmer ciders fight alcopop rivals.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bulmer ciders fight alcopop rivals.

text.p: British cider-maker H.P Bulmer Holdings Plc said on Thursday it had held its own against competition from fashionable "alcopop" drinks that have taken a heavy toll of rival cider firm Matthew Clark.

"Our cider sales in the UK compare reasonably with last year's buoyant and very hot summer, despite May weather being the worst for 50 years," chairman Esmond Bulmer told shareholders at Bulmer's annual meeting.
Bulmer conceded that "alcopops" have established a significant presence but said its own well-established brands had shown resilience.

Alcoholic lemonades and similar alcoholic long drinks have made significant inroads into the British drinks market, which research body Euromonitor said in May would be worth almost 170 million pounds this year after 100 million in 1995.
Matthew Clark Plc stunned the stock market on Monday with a profit warning, citing tough competition from alcopops and a flood of cheap cider products.

The warning has wiped more than 290 million pounds ($451 million) off the company's stock market value since last week. Its shares closed 16p lower at 339-1/2p on Thursday, while Bulmer shares added 15p to close at 567-1.2p.
"It still leaves a lot of questions over exactly what's gone on at Matthew Clark," said an analyst who declined to be named.
"You look at those two statements and they read totally differently to each other. At the moment its very hard to reconcile the two."
Shares in Bulmer were dragged lower earlier this week as analysts anticipated similar problems as at Matthew Clark. Some predicted dire propects for the whole cider industry.
But Bulmer defied pessimists as it said it expected further progress on sales over the year as a whole, subject to its performance in the important Christmas period.
"What they're saying suggests that the cider industry is not heading for a meltdown as orginally thought," said another analyst who did not want to be named.

"They have very effectively distanced themselves from Matthew Clark's problems and made it clear that the problems that Clarks is having with the competition from alcopops is not affecting them," he added.

Bulmer's major brands are more established and do not rely on the same young market as Clarke's. But one analyst said Bulmers was likely to face more competition from fashion-driven products in the future.
"Cider's recent boom will come to a sharp end and Bulmers has just postponed something but cannot avoid it," he said.
Analysts said the future for Matthew Clark shares was more uncertain with one analyst predicting that they would consolidate around the 350p level. ($1=.6430 Pound)
